title: Role Management UI (RBAC v2) — wire notes + permission search/filter behavior
content:
Context / goal
- Rough wire outline for RBAC v2 role management screens in Console.
- Focus: permission viewer + search/filter UX, assignment flows, and how we message denies ("why was I denied?") without leaking sensitive data.
- This doc is intentionally choppy; meant to align Eng + Product + Security quickly.

Assumptions (MVP)
- MVP supports: view roles, create custom role, edit custom role, assign role to user/group/service account, view bindings, view permission details, and basic "why denied" help.
- Role templates exist (generated from YAML in policy bundle); in MVP, templates are selectable but not editable directly (copy-to-custom).
- Scopes in UI (MVP): Org + Project + Environment. Cluster scope appears only if Private is enabled (feature-flag + different wording).
- Deny-by-default. All sensitive endpoints must be annotated; UI should not rely on "hidden" permissions.

Primary personas
- Security Admin: needs least-privilege, separation of duties, visibility into who can do what.
- Platform Operator: needs to fix "permission denied" quickly; wants a crisp way to find required permissions.
- Auditor (read-only): needs ability to review roles/bindings and export audit logs (but not change anything).

Information architecture (left nav)
- Settings (Org) > Access Control
  - Users
  - Groups (if SSO/IdP group mapping enabled)
  - Service Accounts
  - Roles
  - Role Bindings (or "Assignments")
  - Permission Catalog

Page 1: Roles list
Layout
- Header: "Roles"
- Subheader text: "Roles define sets of permissions. Assign roles to users, groups, or service accounts at an org/project/environment scope."
- Primary CTA: [Create role]
- Secondary: [View permission catalog]

Table columns
- Role name (with badge: Template / Custom)
- Scope availability (Org-only vs Org/Project/Env) — computed from permissions included
- # Permissions
- # Assignments (bindings count)
- Last modified (timestamp + actor)
- Kebab menu: View, Edit (custom only), Duplicate, Delete (custom only)

Filters
- Role type: All / Templates / Custom
- Scope: Org / Project / Environment
- Search box: search role name + description

Empty states
- No roles (unlikely). If system fails to load templates, show "Templates unavailable" with retry + status link.

Page 2: Role detail (template or custom)
Header
- Breadcrumb: Access Control > Roles > {RoleName}
- Title row: {RoleName} + badge Template/Custom
- Actions:
  - Template: [Copy to custom role]
  - Custom: [Edit role] [Delete role]

Tabs
1) Permissions
2) Assignments
3) Change history (nice-to-have; can be post-MVP if backend audit trail isn’t ready)

Role detail: Permissions tab
- Top summary:
  - Description (editable for custom)
  - Scope compatibility: "Can be assigned at: Org, Project, Environment" (derived)
  - "Sensitive permissions" count with link to filter them

Permission list UI
- Search input: "Search permissions" (matches permission id, short name, description, resource type)
- Filters (multi-select):
  - Product area: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private / Console / Audit Logs / Billing / Identity
  - Resource type: org, project, environment, deployment, cluster, api_key, secret, routing_policy, audit_log, user, role, role_binding, model, quota
  - Sensitivity: Tier 0 (break-glass only), Tier 1 (high), Tier 2 (medium), Tier 3 (read-only)
  - "Can grant" / "Can revoke" (??? probably not needed; these are separate permissions)
  - "Deprecated" (default hidden)

Permission row
- Left: Permission display name (human-friendly)
- Right: Permission id (monospace): e.g., "console.roles.update" / "controlplane.routing_policy.update" / etc.
- Subtext: short description
- Chips: Resource type, Product area, Sensitivity, Scope constraints (if any)
- Expand caret for details

Permission detail expand panel
- Description (longer)
- Examples: "Used for: editing routing policies, changing model pinning" (but avoid showing internal endpoint names in customer Console)
- Scope: "Org" or "Project" or "Environment" and what the resource key means
- Audit logging: "Actions with this permission are recorded in audit logs" (link to audit logs page)
- Deprecation warning if permission is versioned/deprecated

Notes on search behavior (important)
- Search should be forgiving:
  - tokenized (spaces split terms)
  - case-insensitive
  - supports partial match on permission id segments ("routing" -> routing_policy)
  - supports synonyms ("apikey" -> api_key, "keys" -> api_key)
- Highlight matched substring in both display name and id.
- Performance: do not fetch per-keystroke from backend for large catalogs; do local search on already-fetched permission catalog (assuming <= few thousand).
- When catalogs differ by deployment mode (Hosted vs Private), the UI should show only relevant permissions OR show all but mark "Not available in this deployment".

Page 3: Create role (custom)
Wizard vs single form
- Proposal: single page form with two panels:
  - Left: Role info
  - Right: Permission picker

Role info
- Name (required, unique)
- Description (optional)
- "Start from template" dropdown (optional)
  - Selecting a template pre-populates permissions and disables template itself (since we’re creating a custom copy).

Permission picker panel
- Same search + filters as role detail.
- Two-column picker:
  - Left: all permissions (filtered)
  - Right: selected permissions (with count + quick remove)
- At bottom: computed scope compatibility + warnings.

Warnings (blocking vs non-blocking)
- Blocking:
  - Empty permissions
  - Includes Tier 0 permission (break-glass only) — disallow in standard role creation; show "Contact Support/SecOps" message (internal Console: require extra confirmation + ticket link).
- Non-blocking:
  - Includes high-risk permissions (Tier 1) — show banner "This role can change security-sensitive settings".

Save flow
- [Create role]
- On success: redirect to Role detail.

Page 4: Edit role (custom)
- Same as Create but pre-populated.
- Confirm modal if removing permissions that are currently required by existing role bindings? (Not strictly required, but could cause surprise denies.)
  - Copy: "Removing permissions will immediately restrict actions for assigned principals."
- After save: show "role version" bump? (Backend may have policy bundle versioning; UI just shows updated timestamp + actor.)

Page 5: Assign role (binding)
Entry points
- From Role detail > Assignments tab > [Add assignment]
- From User detail > Roles > [Add role]

Assignment form fields
- Principal type: User / Group / Service Account
- Principal selector (typeahead)
- Scope type: Org / Project / Environment (and Cluster for Private-enabled)
- Scope selector:
  - Org: fixed
  - Project: dropdown of projects
  - Environment: dropdown that depends on project
  - Cluster (Private): dropdown of clusters
- Role selector (role name)

Copy guidance
- Microcopy under scope: "Choose the narrowest scope that still allows the user to do their job."
- If selecting Org scope for a role that’s compatible with narrower scope, show nudge: "This role can be assigned at Project or Environment scope." (non-blocking)

Assignments tab table
- Principal (name + type)
- Scope (Org/Project/Env/Cluster)
- Role
- Created at + actor
- Actions: Remove

Bulk operations (post-MVP)
- Bulk add/remove assignments from CSV.

Page 6: Permission catalog (read-only reference)
Goal
- A searchable catalog for "what permission do I need".

Layout
- Search bar with placeholder: "Search by action (e.g., rotate keys), resource (routing policy), or permission id"
- Filters: same as above
- Results list

Permission detail page
- Similar to permission expand panel but full-page.
- Include "Roles that include this permission" (nice-to-have; may be expensive; could be limited to templates only in MVP)

"Why was I denied?" UX (Console)
Where it shows up
- In error toast/modal when an API call returns 403 with an RBAC v2 denial code.
- Also on a dedicated help page: Access Control > Troubleshooting.

Proposed content in error state
- Title: "You don’t have permission to do that"
- Body:
  - If we can safely provide required permission id: "Required permission: {permission_id}"
  - Show scope context: "Scope: Project {X} / Environment {Y}" if present
  - Show denial reason code (admin only): e.g., "Reason: MISSING_PERMISSION" or "SCOPE_MISMATCH"
  - CTA: [Request access] (opens prefilled message) + [View your roles]

Rules on what we reveal
- For standard users: show a generic description + request access CTA; do not expose internal permission ids unless permission is customer-facing and approved.
- For Org Admin / Security Admin: show permission id + reason code + debug header copyable.
- This must align with PR-28241 denial reason codes + debug header.

Accessibility / usability notes
- Keyboard support for permission picker (arrows + enter to add/remove)
- Ensure chips/filters are screen-reader friendly
- Permission IDs should be copyable (copy icon)
- Avoid long lists without virtualization; permission catalog can be ~500-2000 entries.

Open questions (needs alignment)
1) Scope model UX:
   - Do we show Project/Environment as a single combined selector or two-step? (Preference: two-step for clarity.)
   - How do we represent Cluster for Private without confusing Hosted users? Feature-flag entire section.
2) Group assignments:
   - Are groups always IdP-backed (SCIM) or can we have local groups? Current assumption: IdP-backed for enterprise; local groups optional.
3) Tier 0 permissions:
   - Are any Tier 0 permissions ever assignable in product UI, or only via break-glass workflow? (Security leaning: break-glass only.)
4) "Roles that include this permission":
   - Useful but potentially reveals too much? (Probably okay; it’s within tenant.)
5) Deprecation/versioning:
   - How do we display permission versions? (Maybe hide by default; show only if deprecated.)

Reviewer feedback (captured from quick reviews 1/29–2/11)
- Naomi (PM):
  - "Permission catalog" must be a first-class page; support needs somewhere to point customers.
  - Scope nudge for Org vs Project is good, but keep it non-blocking; customers will intentionally do Org-wide sometimes.
- Marcus (Security Eng):
  - Do not show permission IDs to non-admin users by default.
  - Tier labels should not be scary/opaque; suggest rename "Tier" -> "Risk level" with a tooltip.
  - Strong preference: Tier 0 only via break-glass; UI should block creation/assignment.
- Jordan (Policy engine):
  - Search should match both canonical permission id and aliases; we can ship a synonyms map with the permission registry.
  - For performance, prefer fetching full catalog once and local filtering; catalog should be versioned with policy bundle.
- Kaitlyn (Authn/Authz integration):
  - Denial reason code exposure must match API semantics; some denies may be from gateway vs service (make sure we don’t lie about the source).
  - Consider a dedicated "Debug details" collapsible only for admins.
- Felix (Console):
  - Permission picker needs virtualization; we have other screens that choke on large lists.
  - Avoid expensive "roles that include this permission" query until we have a good index.
- Chloe (Console backend):
  - For assignments, we need a consistent principal identifier (userId/groupId/serviceAccountId). UI should not assume email uniqueness.
  - Change history tab depends on audit event schema; likely post-MVP unless we use audit logs as source.

Next steps
- Tessa/Felix: convert these notes into a minimally clickable prototype (Figma) that covers Roles list -> Role detail -> Create role -> Assign role.
- Chloe/Jordan: confirm which denial reason codes we can surface and which fields are available in the 403 payload for admin users.
- Naomi: confirm MVP scope: do we ship "Role Bindings" page in first release or rely on role/user detail views only?
- Marcus: confirm Tier 0 handling + any language constraints for risk-level tooltips.

Appendix: proposed filter sets (draft)
- Product area filter values:
  - "Console" (UI admin operations)
  - "Control Plane" (org/projects/env/deployments)
  - "API Gateway" (API key ops, routing)
  - "Audit Logs"
  - "Private Deployment" (cluster/installer)
  - "Billing" (invoices, plans)
- Risk level tooltips (draft copy)
  - Low: "Read-only or low-impact actions"
  - Medium: "Operational changes with limited blast radius"
  - High: "Security-sensitive changes (credentials, policies, access)"
  - Critical (break-glass): "Emergency-only permissions controlled by break-glass procedures"
